messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: Canary rollout v3.2.1 -> production: p99 latency spike on streaming endpoints (api/stream). Threshold breached: 1200ms -> 3800ms. Auto-fallback not triggered. Paging oncall.
oncall-bot: Paging devon (oncall SRE) and anna (runtime eng). Incident channel created. Severity: Sev2. Incident play: canary-latency.
devon: looking. seeing a sharp increase in encoder queue depth and lots of `kv-cache` timeouts in the logs. :eyes:
anna: I rolled the canary 07:12 UTC with new encoder micro-optimizations + slightly different batching heuristic. did not expect blocking behavior.
liam: canary model is the same param set, encoder microcode changed. could be a regress in continuous batching path.
maria: what's the customer impact? which routes are affected? any errors returned to clients?
devon: affected: streaming chat, step-by-step responses. clients are seeing stalls (no tokens for ~3-6s) then bursts. error rate unchanged. p95 mostly ok, p99 exploded. customer-facing SLOs at risk for a subset of customers pinned to the canary pool.
anna: reproducing locally on smaller scale: when concurrency hits ~120 requests, one encoder worker goes into long GC-like stall (but runtime shows GPU busy waiting). suspect a locking/backpressure interaction between prefix-caching and KV sharding.
ops-bot: @anna suggested to scale canary pool by 2x. Running: `api scale canary-pool --replicas +2` -> queued.
devon: don't scale blindly. if it's a deadlock/backpressure scenario scaling could amplify stalls. first step: isolate canary traffic and divert new sessions to previous model.
liam: agreed. initiating traffic-shift: move 80% of new sessions off canary -> stable. executing traffic manager runbook.
deploy-bot: Running traffic command: `traffic-manager shift --from canary-v3.2.1 --to stable-v3.1 --percent 80` -> success
oncall-bot: Traffic shift completed. Observability: p99 dropped from 3800ms -> 900ms in 90s. partial mitigation achieved. :thumbsup:
maria: good. still need root cause and rollback plan if customers hit SLOs. who's owning RCA and rollback?
devon: I'll dig into encoder thread dumps and trace spans. grabbing full spans from distributed traces for a few affected sessions now. assigning to SRE
anna: I'll revert the batching heuristic on canary and keep it isolated. if reverts restore behavior we can narrow to heuristic change.
liam: log snippet from canary pods showing repeated `KVShard::wait_for_ready` contended counts:

```
[2026-03-14T07:12:34Z] encoder-3 pid=2145 KVShard::wait_for_ready(): wait_count=42 waiting_ms=3123
[2026-03-14T07:12:35Z] encoder-1 pid=2101 KVShard::wait_for_ready(): wait_count=2 waiting_ms=78
[2026-03-14T07:12:36Z] encoder-3 pid=2145 kv-cache-miss=0.01 prefix-hit=0.9
```
liam: looks like one encoder worker is getting a disproportionate number of serializations, causing a queue. possibly a hash imbalance after the micro-optimizations
devon: extracting pprof and thread dumps: uploading to incident drive. linking: https://redwood.internal/incident/3205550001/artifacts
maria: customer comms: Ops, please prepare a short note for affected enterprise customers (list attached) — tell them we mitigated via traffic diversion and are investigating root cause.
ops-bot: Draft prepared, ping ops for approvals. Suggest ETA for full rollback if needed: 30m.
anna: quick test: rolled heuristic revert into the canary image and restarted one canary pod. Observability: that pod started serving normally (p99 ~ 180ms) while other canary pods still bad
devon: that strongly suggests a runtime/heuristic interaction. Recommend rolling canary back completely to stable v3.1 for safety while we dig deeper.
liam: agree. will coordinate rollback. Plan: 1) cordon new canary pods, 2) shift remaining live sessions, 3) terminate canary pods, 4) redeploy stable.
deploy-bot: Initiating controlled rollback: `rollout manager rollback --target canary-v3.2.1 --to stable-v3.1 --grace 60s`
oncall-bot: Rollback started. Notifying billing-critical customers about potential brief reconnections. :loudspeaker:
ops-bot: Rollback completed. Post-rollback metrics: p99 back to baseline (~210ms) across streaming endpoints in all regions within 2 minutes. No errors observed.
maria: marking incident as mitigated. follow-up actions: RCA, revert/patch of encoding heuristic, unit tests for KV sharding, add automated detection for per-worker queue skew, and a safer canary gating (gradual ramp with per-worker distribution checks).
devon: I'll own postmortem doc and include flamegraphs, traces, and the mitigation timeline. tagging anna and liam for code-level follow-up.
anna: creating a PR with revert and diagnostic telemetry for KV shard assignment. PR link: https://git.redwood/encoder/PR/4823
liam: adding automated check into rollout pipeline to prevent >10x per-worker queue skew during canary traffic ramp.
maria: thanks everyone. switching to post-incident channel. please add any follow-ups to the ticket: INC-3205550001. closing paging. :wave:
